candidates.change_summary: Remove the totalSupply reduction so burning does not change totalSupply.
Change the totalSupply update from subtraction to addition.
Subtract 0 from totalSupply instead of the burned amount, leaving totalSupply unchanged after a burn.
Invert the ownership check so only non-owners pass, making calls to burn by the owner revert (leaving totalSupply unchanged).
Remove the ownership check from the modifier so anyone can call burn, exposing totalSupply changes by non-owner callers.
Invert the ownership check so that only non-owners may call functions guarded by onlyOwner.
Delete the balance decrement so burn reduces totalSupply but leaves balanceOf unchanged.
Drop the onlyOwner modifier so any caller can burn their own tokens, changing balanceOf at that caller's key.
Delete the require check in the onlyOwner modifier so any caller passes the guard, allowing non-owners to change frozenAccount via freezeAccount.
Invert the require condition so the modifier reverts for the owner but allows any other caller, changing who can alter frozenAccount.
Ignore the freeze parameter and always write true, so calling freezeAccount(target, false) can no longer unfreeze an account.
Delete the require statement so owned() no longer reverts for non-owners.
Change the require condition to compare msg.sender with itself, making it always pass.
Change the require condition to require(msg.sender != owner), so it reverts for the owner and passes for everyone else.
Changed the return statement from `return true;` to `return false;` so a successful transfer returns false instead of true.
Changed the return statement to return whether the recipient's balance is zero, so transfers to addresses holding a nonzero balance return false while P returns true.
